answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a fixed amount of scarce, withdrawable-after-a-delay stake before it can earn from tasks. When a randomly selected peer checks a task, cryptographic evidence of duplicated submissions lets the protocol slash the offending stake and reward the checker. Creating a hundred fake agents then requires a hundred deposits, not just a hundred names; the attacker ties up capital and risks losing it. A tide of accounts cannot cheaply hide behind a willow or trellis of aliases.
